title: Modern JavaScript ES6+ and Modules — Project

pool_config.pool_brief: Build a data processing system using modern ES6+ JavaScript features. Your solution must use: object destructuring (including nested and with renaming), array destructuring, spread operator for arrays (copy, merge) and objects (copy, add properties immutably), rest parameters in at least one function, default parameters, and a pipeline combining destructuring with array HOFs (map/filter with destructured parameters). All variables must use const or let.

projects.title: Flutterwave Merchant Analytics Pipeline
projects.scenario: Build a merchant analytics system for Flutterwave using modern JavaScript features. Process the provided transaction dataset using destructuring, spread, rest, and ES6+ patterns to generate reports immutably.
requirements: Use object destructuring to extract merchant name, country, and nested plan details (plan.name, plan.fee) from a merchant config object; log each extracted value
Use array destructuring to extract the first two transactions and collect the rest into a 'remaining' variable using rest syntax; log all three
Use the spread operator to create a copy of the transactions array, then create a new array merging transactions from two different merchants (without mutating originals)
Use the spread operator on objects to create an updated merchant object with an added 'lastUpdated' property and changed 'status' — without mutating the original; log both to prove immutability

Write a function with rest parameters `calculateFees(...amounts)` that accepts any number of amounts and returns total fees (1.5% each); also write a function with a default parameter for the fee rate
Build a pipeline: use map with destructured parameters ({amount, status}) to add a fee property, then filter with destructuring to keep only successful transactions, then log the results

projects.title: Paystack Payment Dashboard Builder
projects.scenario: Build a payment dashboard data processor for Paystack using modern JavaScript features. Transform and filter payment records using destructuring, spread, rest, and ES6+ patterns.
requirements: Use object destructuring to extract business name, email, and nested settings (settings.currency, settings.webhook) from a business config object; log each
Use array destructuring to extract the first payment and collect the rest; log the first payment's id and the count of remaining
Use spread to create an immutable sorted copy of payments (by amount descending) without mutating the original; log both to prove immutability
Use spread on objects to create a new business config with added 'updatedAt' and overridden 'settings.currency' — without mutating; log both
Write a function `formatAmounts(currency = '₦', ...amounts)` with a default parameter and rest; return formatted strings like '₦5,000'
Build a pipeline: map with destructured parameters to add a formattedAmount property, filter with destructuring to keep amount > 3000, forEach with destructuring to log results

projects.title: Bolt Trip Data Processor
projects.scenario: Build a trip data processor for Bolt using modern JavaScript features. Analyse driver and trip data using destructuring, spread, rest, and ES6+ patterns for immutable transformations.
requirements: Use object destructuring to extract driver name, rating, and nested vehicle details (vehicle.make, vehicle.plate) from a driver object; log each
Use array destructuring to extract the first and last trips from the array (use length - 1 for last); log both trip IDs
Use spread to merge two trip arrays (morning trips and evening trips) into one combined array without mutating either; log the combined length
Use spread on objects to create an updated driver object with added 'lastOnline' date and changed 'status' — log both original and updated to prove immutability
Write a function `tripSummary(driverName, ...distances)` using rest to collect all distances; return total distance and average; use a default parameter for the unit ('km')
Build a pipeline: map with destructured parameters to add fare (distance × 150), filter with destructuring to keep completed trips only, forEach to log formatted results

projects.title: Publica Academy Student Data Transformer
projects.scenario: Build a student data transformer for Publica Academy using modern JavaScript features. Process enrolment and grade data using destructuring, spread, rest, and ES6+ patterns.
requirements: Use object destructuring to extract student name, email, and nested enrolment details (enrolment.cohort, enrolment.startDate) from a student record; log each
Use array destructuring with skip syntax to extract the 1st and 3rd modules from a modules array; collect remaining with rest; log all
Use spread to create a new modules array that adds a new module at the beginning and one at the end — without mutating the original; log both arrays' lengths
Use spread on objects to create a graded student object that adds a 'grade' and 'graduated' property to the original student — without mutating; log both
Write a function `calculateAverage(studentName, ...scores)` using rest; return the average; use a default parameter for minimum passing score (50)
Build a pipeline: map with destructured parameters to add a passed boolean (score >= 50), filter with destructuring to keep only passed, forEach to log name and score

projects.title: Jumia Product Catalogue Transformer
projects.scenario: Build a product catalogue data transformer for Jumia using modern JavaScript features. Process inventory data using destructuring, spread, rest, and ES6+ patterns for immutable operations.
requirements: Use object destructuring to extract product name, price, and nested seller details (seller.name, seller.rating) from a product object; log each
Use array destructuring to extract the first two products and rest from the inventory array; log each group
Use spread to merge two category arrays (electronics and clothing) into a combined catalogue without mutating; then use spread to add a product at index 0
Use spread on objects to create a discounted product with added 'discount' and recalculated 'salePrice' properties — without mutating; log both
Write a function `createBundle(bundleName, ...products)` using rest that returns an object with name, items (the products), and itemCount; use a default parameter for discount percentage
Build a pipeline: map with destructured parameters to add VAT (price × 1.075), filter with destructuring to keep inStock only, forEach with destructuring to log product name and VAT price

descriptors.full: Object destructuring extracts nested properties correctly; array destructuring uses skip and rest syntax; destructuring used in function parameters within HOF callbacks
descriptors.partial: Basic destructuring present but no nested or no array destructuring

descriptors.full: Spread used to copy/merge arrays immutably; spread used to copy/extend objects without mutation; original data unchanged (demonstrated with logs)
descriptors.partial: Spread used on arrays OR objects but not both, or mutation still occurring

descriptors.full: At least one function uses rest parameters (...args) to accept variable arguments; at least one function uses a default parameter value; both produce correct results
descriptors.partial: Rest or default used but not both, or used incorrectly
descriptors.none: No rest parameters and no default parameters

descriptors.full: const/let used; at least one HOF pipeline uses destructuring in callbacks; immutability proven with console logs; output is clear and labelled
descriptors.partial: Pipeline present but doesn't use destructured parameters
descriptors.none: var used, no pipeline, or output is unclear
